objective: Run a bounded, zero-experiment, non-batch review asking two questions the thirteen-round trigger-search pattern raised but no single round was scoped to ask: (1) whether the frozen pre-admission gate's G2 and G8 items -- the two items every near-miss across all thirteen rounds has failed on -- are calibrated correctly, or whether they structurally foreclose essentially every known technique family for sub-Theta(B^3) polynomial-remainder construction regardless of merit; and (2) whether H-CREP-001/EXP-CREP-001's constructor-vs-witness framing of the P1553 remainder problem should be revisited or narrowed, given the accumulated evidence base (EV-CRYPTO-002's eight-route falsification plus thirteen further disjoint-literature negative searches) may now support a scoped, checkable structural argument for why any public sub-Theta(B^3) constructor for r_R mod g_I would have to defeat both convergent failure modes simultaneously. This produces no experiment, implementation, B71, scientific transition, speedup, attack, or breakthrough claim -- it may produce a scoped structural argument (a proof-shaped analysis, not a new run) if one is genuinely available, or a considered finding that the gate/framing are appropriately calibrated as-is.

tasks.title: Gate-calibration and framing-revisit review: is G2/G8 miscalibrated, and does the accumulated 13-round evidence support a structural argument?

handoff.objective: Assess, without running any experiment, whether the frozen pre-admission gate's G2/G8 items are calibrated correctly given thirteen rounds of convergent failure evidence, and whether H-CREP-001/EXP-CREP-001's constructor-vs-witness framing should be revisited, narrowed, or left as-is; if the accumulated evidence genuinely supports a scoped, checkable structural argument for why any public sub-Theta(B^3) constructor for r_R mod g_I must defeat both convergent failure modes simultaneously, state it precisely with a proof-shaped decomposition; if it does not, say so and name exactly what additional evidence would be needed.
handoff.uncertainty_reduced: Two linked but distinct uncertainties: (1) Gate calibration -- is G2's 'no roots, factors, witnesses, support tables, or source enumeration' clause and G8's already-costed-route exclusion an appropriately strict filter for a genuine sub-Theta(B^3) public constructor, or does it (perhaps unintentionally) exclude entire classes of legitimate approaches by definition rather than by their actual failure to construct r_R mod g_I? Answer by finding, if any exists, a hypothetical or real technique that would satisfy the problem's actual requirement (a public, cheap, correct r_R mod g_I) but would be wrongly excluded by G2 or G8 as currently worded -- if none can be found after genuine effort, that is itself informative and should be recorded as a considered finding, not a default. (2) Framing revisit -- does the pattern of exactly two convergent failure modes (Theta(B^3) materialization; equivalent-witness circularity) across thirteen disjoint literatures constitute sufficient evidence for a scoped structural claim (e.g., 'any public sub-Theta(B^3) constructor for r_R mod g_I over the frozen complete-chart setting must be either an already-costed materialization or require a witness/oracle, because of [named structural reason]'), or is thirteen rounds of literature screening categorically insufficient evidence for any such claim regardless of the pattern's consistency (a 'we haven't found one yet' fallacy)? If a structural argument is genuinely available, it must be scoped, checkable, and carry the same rigor as any proof-oriented proposal under docs/inventor-protocol.md Section 8 (a proof_search_map with exact baseline reproduction, observation-collision search, quantifier-order statement, and method ceiling with a nearby-object control) -- this is a claim about the shape of the search space, not a new experiment, and it does NOT itself close H-CREP-001 or reject the underlying problem; it would at most inform how future pre-admission rounds are scoped.
inputs: docs/inventor-protocol.md (Section 8's proof-architecture portfolio applies if a structural argument is proposed)
docs/claims-and-verification.md (claim tiers -- a structural argument about the search space is NOT a solve/relation and carries no certificate obligation, but must still be scoped exactly)

ledger/goals/GOAL-ECDLP-001/goal.yaml (the live next_action opening this task, the frozen gate text in next_action_superseded_20260828_standing_directive, and all thirteen trigger-search terminal notes -- read every one, this task requires synthesizing across all of them, not just the most recent)
ledger/hypotheses/H-CREP-001.yaml (the constructor-vs-witness framing this task is asked to assess)
experiments/EXP-CREP-001/specification.yaml (the eight named ROUTE-01 through ROUTE-08 already-costed routes that G8 excludes against)
ledger/evidence/EV-CRYPTO-002.yaml (the eight-route falsification evidence this task's framing-revisit question builds on)
all thirteen prior trigger-search round packets and the six terminal pre-admission packets named in read_scope (the full evidentiary record this synthesis is over)
knowledge/ and inputs/ (internal corpus for a resource-check pass on whether any known technique is wrongly excluded by the gate)
constraints: This is a non-batch, zero-experiment review task, same discipline as the thirteen trigger-search rounds. Do not create B71, BATCH, IDEA, EV, DEC, CORR, experiment, implementation, status transition, speedup, attack, SOTA, or breakthrough records or claims. Do not open any family pre-admission intake. Do not change H-CREP-001's status or EXP-CREP-001's specification -- this task assesses framing, it does not itself amend a frozen contract; a Coordinator decision would be required for any actual change, and this task does not make one.

This task must genuinely attempt to find a counterexample to G2/G8's calibration -- a real or hypothetical technique that would legitimately solve the stated problem (public, cheap, correct r_R mod g_I from E, P, Q alone) but is wrongly excluded by the gate's current wording. A search that only re-confirms 'everything we tried failed the gate' without genuinely trying to construct a counterexample to the GATE ITSELF (as opposed to the problem) has not answered question (1); if no counterexample is found after real effort, say so explicitly as a considered finding with the specific attempts made, not as a default non-answer.

Any structural argument proposed for question (2) must be scoped EXACTLY: name the precise premises (which properties of the frozen complete-chart system, g_I, r_R are load-bearing), the precise conclusion (what class of constructors is excluded and why), and must NOT overclaim beyond the thirteen rounds' actual literature coverage -- a structural argument that both failure modes are exhaustive for 'all possible techniques' is almost certainly overclaiming; a structural argument scoped to 'every technique in the four literatures searched, and structurally-similar techniques sharing the same input requirements' is the honest ceiling. If the accumulated evidence is judged insufficient for any structural claim, say so and name what would change that judgment.
No commands, programs, experiments, benchmarks, computer algebra, or implementation. The one maximum run is the bounded inference session only; experiment_maximum_runs is zero.

Controls before belief applies here too: any proposed structural argument must be run against a nearby object for which the argument's conclusion is KNOWN FALSE (the proves-too-much control) -- e.g. does the same argument, applied to a setting where a public sub-Theta(B^3) constructor for an analogous quantity IS known to exist (if one can be identified), incorrectly predict impossibility there too? If so, the argument is broken and must say so.

Citation provenance is mandatory. Every source carries recalled | retrieved | kb | internal. A recalled source is a pointer telling a reviewer where to look and can never back a claim until retrieved and read by an authorized agent in a new record.

Write the four substantive artifacts first and runtime-session-receipt.json last. Do not alter any input, goal, ledger, prior pre-admission, prior round, or queue file. YAML hygiene is mandatory and will be independently re-checked with a strict parser (Gate 6): no plain scalar may contain an embedded, unescaped double-quote or a colon-followed-by-space -- wrap the ENTIRE scalar in single quotes if either is needed. No duplicated top-level keys at any nesting level. This exact defect class broke artifacts in two of the last three rounds; check every free-text field before finishing.
deliverables: gate-calibration-analysis.yaml: a direct answer to question (1). State whether a genuine counterexample to G2/G8's calibration was found (a technique that legitimately solves the problem but is wrongly excluded) or not, with the specific candidate techniques actually tried against this question (not the thirteen rounds' original candidates re-litigated, but a fresh attempt to construct a gate-defeating counterexample). If a miscalibration is found, propose the exact corrected gate wording and what it would newly admit. If none is found, record the considered finding and what would change it.

framing-revisit-analysis.yaml: a direct answer to question (2). If a scoped structural argument is proposed, state its exact premises, conclusion, and scope boundary, plus the proves-too-much control result. If no structural argument is judged supportable, say so and name the missing evidence. Either way, state explicitly whether H-CREP-001's constructor-vs-witness framing should be revisited, narrowed, or left as-is, and why -- this is a recommendation to a future Coordinator decision, not itself a status change.

proof-search-map.yaml: the four audits from docs/inventor-protocol.md Section 8, applied to any structural argument proposed in framing-revisit-analysis.yaml (exact baseline reproduction of what the argument claims to establish, observation-collision search against all thirteen rounds and the eight named routes, quantifier-order statement, method ceiling with the proves-too-much nearby-object control); if no structural argument is proposed, each audit records why it does not apply.

source-novelty-audit.yaml: provenance-labelled sources (recalled | retrieved | kb | internal) for every source consulted in reaching both analyses, with an exact internal overlap audit against all thirteen trigger-search rounds, the six terminal pre-admission packets, H-CREP-001, and EXP-CREP-001.

runtime-session-receipt.json: written last, binding exact artifacts and hashes available to the producing runtime, requested and resolved inference provenance, reasoning effort, fallback and degradation state, model verification state, zero experiments, and any operational limitation without treating it as mathematical evidence.

The claim ceiling is a considered analytical finding and, at most, a scoped structural argument about the search space -- never a status change to H-CREP-001 or EXP-CREP-001, never a B71, experiment, evidence, ECDLP attack, SOTA movement, or breakthrough.
completion_gate: Gate 1: question (1) is answered with a genuine, disclosed attempt to construct a gate-defeating counterexample, not a re-litigation of the thirteen rounds' original findings.

Gate 2: question (2) is answered with either a precisely scoped structural argument (premises, conclusion, scope boundary, proves-too-much control) or an explicit statement of insufficient evidence and what would change that.

Gate 3: any proposed structural argument passes docs/inventor-protocol.md Section 8's four audits, each recorded in proof-search-map.yaml, with a genuine proves-too-much control result (not merely asserted to pass).
Gate 4: the source-novelty audit separates retrieved from recalled from internal and names the internal overlap audit against all thirteen rounds, six screened packets, H-CREP-001, and EXP-CREP-001.
Gate 5: no B71, experiment, implementation, status transition, or claim beyond the ceiling is created or asserted.
Gate 6: every YAML artifact parses under a strict, unforgiving parser (no embedded unescaped quotes in plain scalars, no duplicated top-level keys at any nesting level).

If any gate is unmet the task fails its completion gate and the Coordinator takes a scoped repair; failing to find a counterexample or a structural argument is not itself evidence of anything beyond this task's own search.
